digest.component_or_area: tickets-branch history reclamation and pack shrinkage
propositions: The blobless CI-guarded checkout pack is 481 MiB (vs 100 MiB budget); `.retired` GC alone shrinks it ~0 because `.retired` files are blobs and the guarded pack contains zero blobs.

Below-horizon commit/tree collapse (not `.retired` tombstone removal) is the only lever to shrink the blobless pack; max safe shrink at N=30d is ~365–380 MiB (still above budget); achieving ≤100 MiB requires an unsafe <4-day horizon.

A remote-anchored eligibility boundary (C1–C5) — folded by horizon-aged SNAPSHOT, folding commit reachable from remote ≥N days, stale clones forced-overridden, authorship carried/grandfathered, no unfolded dependence — provably preserves I1–I9 invariants under the accepted >N-day loss.

Stale-clone forced override (reset >N-day offline clones to remote on reconnect) converts the probabilistic remote-horizon from "no clone should partition >N days" to an enforced invariant, closing the I1 resurrection hole.

History rewrite emits new baseline via core-git `git fast-import`, re-signs SNAPSHOT, re-resolves authorship_ledger positions against new graph, re-anchors `enforce_since` to baseline; per-backend publish-swap uses git-ref `--force-with-lease` CAS for git remotes and S3 exclusive bundle-set replacement (auto-doctor bypass) for the S3 backend.

A temporary W3 budget bridge (raise REBAR_CHECKOUT_PACK_LIMIT_KIB ~550 MiB) is unavoidable to unblock the health lane near-term, paired with structural W1 (batch enrichment+digest writes) and W2 (shard 6,008-flat root-tree) fixes for durability; ADR 0106 + S0–S3 tooling define the contract; S1–S3 shadow-clone dry-run must pass verify-authorship + pack-shrink validation before any prod rewrite.
